rules.statement: When an end-user account is disabled or deleted, end all of its principal's sessions through the session termination seam with a reason that names the cause, rather than revoking grants or tokens directly.
rules.why: Revoking grants without the termination seam sends no back-channel logout to relying parties and leaves the termination unaudited, and if sessions stay in place a refresh token of a disabled or deleted account can still be redeemed until it expires.
rules.check: Look for account disable/delete code paths that skip session termination, or that delete grants/refresh tokens directly instead of calling the session service's revoke-all with a specific termination reason.

rules.statement: When deleting an account or principal, terminate its sessions before removing the account, identity, principal, grants or consents, so the sessions can still be listed and their relying parties notified.
rules.why: Once the deletion commits, the grants are erased and can no longer be listed to send back-channel logout to the relying parties.
rules.check: In a deletion flow, check that session termination runs after validation but before any removal or save that erases the principal's grants or sessions.

rules.statement: Disabling an account must keep its consents, and deleting a principal must erase its consents and grants as well as its role assignments.
rules.why: Disabling can be undone, so removing consents would make the end user consent again. A deleted principal should leave no consent or grant behind.
rules.check: Look for disable paths that remove consents, and for principal removal code that leaves consents or grants of that principal in the tenant.

rules.statement: The authorization request and every grant that issues tokens for a subject must check the subject's account standing, and must refuse with access_denied when the local account is disabled or no longer exists.
rules.why: Otherwise a refresh token or other grant of a deleted or disabled account keeps being redeemed until it expires.
rules.check: Look for new or changed token-issuing grant handlers that skip subject validation, and for subject-validation handlers that let a missing or disabled self-issued account through or return an error code other than access_denied.

rules.statement: A chained validation handler that runs after other handlers must return at once when the operation already has an error, and must not overwrite that error.
rules.why: The account check runs after the default handler and must leave an earlier refusal as it is.
rules.check: Look for later-priority validation handlers that do work or set an error without first checking whether the operation already has one.

rules.statement: Blocking or disabling an end user must block the principal across all of its connections, not only the connection whose account was disabled, while a subject the account source cannot judge (no self-issued identity or self-issuer claim) must not be refused.
rules.why: A block on only the local connection would let the principal keep signing in through another connection, and the core cannot tell a deleted principal from one that never had a local account.
rules.check: Check that the account check refuses the principal whenever any of its self-issued accounts is disabled or missing, and that subjects with only external identities and no self-issuer claim are not refused.
